notes:
Method: downloaded the official PG catalogue CSV (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/feeds/pg_catalog.csv, 2026-10-13) and filtered Language = 'la' (103 items) plus multilingual records containing 'la' (c. 45 items, mostly 'en; la'); then fetched each candidate's landing page with curl (HTTP 200) and HEAD-checked the download redirects. The browse page https://www.gutenberg.org/browse/languages/la (HTTP 200) lists c. 360 links but the catalogue CSV is the authoritative list. IMPORTANT: many Latin texts with English apparatus are catalogued as Language 'English' or 'English; Latin' (e.g. Ritchie #8997, D'Ooge #18251, Bennett #15665), so the Latin language filter alone misses them.
URL patterns (all verified for every entry above): landing https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/NNNN (200); EPUB3 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/NNNN.epub3.images -> 302 -> https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/NNNN/pgNNNN-images-3.epub (200, application/epub+zip); EPUB2 no images .../NNNN.epub.noimages -> .../pgNNNN.epub (200, checked on the first 8 teaching books); HTML .../NNNN.html.images -> 302 -> http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/NNNN/pgNNNN-images.html (200, text/html); plain text .../NNNN.txt.utf-8 -> .../pgNNNN.txt (200, text/plain). Kindle (.kf8/.kindle) also exists. Project Gutenberg does NOT provide PDF for any of these items.
License: https://www.gutenberg.org/policy/license.html (HTTP 200). PG states its ebooks are 'not restricted by copyright in the United States' and 'if you are not located in the United States you'll have to check the laws of the country where you are located'. PG no longer uses the term 'public domain'. Redistribution is free (the license allows copying, giving away, derivative works); the PG trademark may not be used for commercial redistribution without permission, and the license header must be kept or all PG references stripped. For Brazil (70 years p.m.a.) I computed status from the author/editor death years printed on the PG landing pages: hosting_allowed=false was set for Puer romanus and Pons tironum (W. H. S. Jones d. 1963 -> 2034), Oxford Book of Latin Verse (Garrod d. 1960 -> 2031), and for editions whose editor's death year is not given on PG (Nall #25861, Upcott #39355, Tyler #9090, Arnold #33197). All other entries are PD in Brazil on the stated death years.
Audio: PG itself hosts no audio for these texts except #19635 (LibriVox, Psalm 22, Vulgate) which is audio-only; LibriVox recordings should be verified by the LibriVox agent, not from PG.
Caveat on macronised editions #70468/#73030/#74851/#70713: the macrons were added 2022-2024 by a PG volunteer ('Aurēliānus Agricola') and the files are released under the PG license like any other PG ebook; the underlying works are 16th-19th-century.
Duplicates: #826 and #827 are both 'Latin Vulgate, Esther' in the catalogue; only #826 was verified.
author_death_year is null for ancient (BCE) authors; for annotated editions the relevant modern editor death years are given in editor_or_annotator / editor_remarks.
